root_cause_label: Agent treated /usr/bin/python3 (3.11.2) as the system Python to fix, never checking that the benchmark targets Python 3.13; it then installed fasttext+downgraded numpy under Python 3.11 instead of patching the existing fasttext/FastText.py under /usr/local/lib/python3.13
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent assumed /usr/bin/python3 (3.11.2) was the relevant system Python and built a working fasttext setup there via numpy downgrade, completely bypassing the required one-line patch to the Python 3.13 fasttext installation that the benchmark actually tests.
t_err_evidence: Step 6: agent runs '/usr/bin/python3 -c import sys; print(...)' and discovers Python 3.11.2, then adopts this interpreter as the target to fix without verifying what Python version the benchmark or pytest uses; the actual benchmark target is Python 3.13 at /usr/local/lib/python3.13.
t_commit_evidence: Step 11: agent runs 'apt update && apt install -y python3-pip' to bootstrap pip for /usr/bin/python3 (3.11), committing to a multi-step installation path for the wrong interpreter that forecloses patching the correct Python 3.13 fasttext install.
trigger_explanation: At step 6, the agent identified /usr/bin/python3 (3.11.2) as 'the system Python' without checking the task specification or the actual interpreter used by the benchmark. The benchmark requires patching fasttext under Python 3.13 (at /usr/local/lib/python3.13), but the agent never looked for Python 3.13 or read the solution requirements before choosing its target interpreter.
fabrication_evidence: Starting at step 11, agent installs fasttext and numpy on /usr/bin/python3 (3.11.2) and at step 21 downgrades numpy to 1.26.4 to make predict() work; step 22 shows agent's own test passing. However, benchmark pytest targets Python 3.13 and expects the one-line patch to /usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/fasttext/FastText.py; the agent's solution on Python 3.11 never addresses the actual benchmark path.
